en.title: Global Macro — A Fed pause, a Canadian hike and a steeper Treasury curve expose the cost of persistent energy inflation
en.deck: The Fed held 3.75–4.00% with two dissents while Canada raised rates; US long yields rose despite a softer two-year yield, revealing divergent responses to energy inflation and financing needs.
en.regime: Monetary-policy divergence and long-duration funding pressure amid persistent energy inflation.
en.key_risk: Fuel-cost pass-through and duration-financing needs tighten credit conditions without a further Fed rate increase.
watch: US Q3 GDP advance and September personal income/outlays release
ECB and Bank of Japan 29 October decisions
US Treasury 10Y–2Y curve and long-term issuance
US distillate inventories and fuel-price pass-through

pt-BR.title: Global Macro — Pausa do Fed, alta de juros no Canadá e inclinação da curva americana revelam o custo da inflação energética persistente
pt-BR.deck: O Fed manteve juros de 3,75% a 4,00%, com duas dissidências, enquanto o Canadá elevou a taxa; rendimentos longos dos Treasuries subiram apesar da queda no papel de dois anos.
pt-BR.regime: Divergência de política monetária e encarecimento do financiamento longo em meio à inflação energética persistente.
pt-BR.key_risk: Repasse dos combustíveis e necessidades de financiamento longo restringem o crédito mesmo sem nova alta de juros pelo Fed.
watch: PIB preliminar do terceiro trimestre e renda/gastos pessoais de setembro nos EUA

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 2026-10-29 05:00 BRT (08:00 UTC). Completed 28 Oct US/Canada sessions and releases; 29 Oct ECB, BOJ, US GDP and PCE not yet released.
producer_checks.novelty: Compared 26–28 Oct public MT-GM editions. New 28 Oct FOMC 10–2 hold and Canadian first hike since July 2023; 27–28 Oct US yield-curve bear steepening; 28 Oct ICI weekly flow vintage and EIA stocks. Earlier AI memory contracts, Australian CPI and Brazil post-election repricing are background.
producer_checks.source_check: 14 dated numbered references per locale, predominantly official Fed, BoC, US Treasury, ABS, RBNZ, ICI, ECB, BEA and EIA; Reuters used for closing prices and EIA-vintage cross-check.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Both editions have 1 dated 10Y Treasury chart (26/27/28 Oct), 1 fund-flow bar chart (21 Oct week), 1 six-row policy table, 1 two-chain causal flow and 1 five-region map; numeric values/units identical.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: Identical 14 reference URLs and dates; matched 10Y yields 5.00/4.99/5.05, fund flows -33.50/+45.82/+12.32, monetary policy levels, EIA inventory observations, caveats and information cutoff.
producer_checks.research_depth: EN ~2512 words; PT-BR ~2899 words, including references.

contrary_evidence: US equities advanced modestly on 28 Oct, contradicting a blanket risk-off reading.
ICI combined fund flows were positive for the earlier 21 Oct week, despite mutual-fund outflows.
NZ held narrowly and Australian underlying inflation is not identical to headline inflation; tightening is not globally synchronized.
limitations: The 29 Oct ECB, BOJ, GDP and personal-income/outlays releases are after cutoff.
The dynamic EIA weekly page did not consistently expose the 28 Oct vintage, so its figures were cross-checked with contemporaneous Reuters reporting.
No verified 28 Oct issuer-level financing or complete cross-border investor flow dataset; yield changes cannot be decomposed into term premium and inflation expectations.
Market settlements and official daily par yields are distinct instruments and observation times.
